## Tutorials Test your understanding of HTML images by completing this coding challenge. ## Tutorials Complete each step in the editor and watch the result as your page takes shape. ## Tutorials A favicon is a small image displayed next to the page title in the browser tab. You can use any image you like as your favicon. You can also create your own favicon on sites likehttps://www.favicon.cc. A favicon image is displayed to the left of the page title in the browser tab, like this: To add a favicon to your website, either save your favicon image to the root directory of your webserver, or create a folder in the root directory called images, and save your favicon image in this folder. A common name for a favicon image is "favicon.ico". Next, add aelement to your "index.html" file, after theelement, like this: Now, save the "index.html" file and reload it in your browser. Your browser tab should now display your favicon image to the left of the page title. The following table shows the file format support for a favicon image: ### Code Examples ``` <!DOCTYPE html> <html> <head> <title>My Page Title

This is a Heading

This is a paragraph.

``` ## Tutorials Test what you have learned about HTML favicon. ## Tutorials Every web page should have a page title to describe the meaning of the page. Theelement adds a title to your page: The title should describe the content and the meaning of the page. The page title is very important for search engine optimization (SEO). The text is used by search engine algorithms to decide the order when listing pages in search results. The<title>element: So, try to make the title as accurate and meaningful as possible! ### Code Examples ``` <!DOCTYPE html> <html> <head> <title>HTML Tutorial The content of the document...... ``` ---
